text.p: Second seed Goran Ivanisevic sounded a warning to his Wimbledon rivals with a ruthless exhibition of power serving on Monday to charge into the second round.

On a gloomy opening day to the championships, thunder reverberated around court two -- both from the skies and the Croat's racket -- as Ivanisevic took just 64 minutes to brush past Romania's Dinu Pescariu 6-1 6-3 6-3.
Ivanisevic, twice a losing Wimbledon finalist, hammered 24 aces and barely raised a sweat against his 106th ranked opponent, surrendering just a handful points on his own service.

The big serving Croat characteristically stuttered on his opening service game, serving two double-faults but hit the target with consecutive aces to level the score at 1-1 and never looked back, taking the next five games to clinch the set.
Ivanisevic, who headed the ace list on the men's tour last year, needed just 19 minutes to take the second set, Pescariu stealing only one point from his rival's serve, courtesy of a double-fault.
The Croat, ranked three in the world, finished the set in the same manner he started it, firing four straight aces past his increasingly despondent opponent.

The tall left-hander seemed at times to toy with the Romanian, charging his service and dictating the terms from the net. He cruelly forced Pescariu to scamper from one corner of the court to the other with some deft volleying, but occasionally decided against a torture session opting instead to unwind his ferocious forehand.
Pescariu dropped his opening serve in the third set and valiantly held on to his next three service games and even managed to acquire a break point against Ivanisevic.

Heavy clouds and rumbling thunder inspired the Croat to up the tempo and save the pair a return journey. Just as light rain started to fall, Ivanisevic sealed the tie with his second match point thanks to a backhand winner.
